headline: Connor Hellebuyck addresses Jets fans for first time since trade to Devils
take:
The Athletic reports that Connor Hellebuyck, now with the Devils, addressed Jets fans for the first time since the trade, breaking his silence in an Instagram post about his decision to request a move out of Winnipeg.

The numbers say New Jersey is doing fine around him. The Devils are 10-5-0 and generate 58.6 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season, with a strong 5-on-5 share of 58 percent. Hellebuyck's own start is the soft spot: three games, a .900 save percentage, and goals saved above expected of -0.54, meaning he has let in about half a goal more than an average goalie would have on the same shots. That is a tiny sample, and last season he was 3.43 goals better than expected over 57 games. Winnipeg, at 5-8-3, creates only 45.7 percent of the expected goals and has scored 9.6 fewer goals than its chances suggest. Its goaltending is roughly average (-0.1), so the Jets' problems sit mostly in play and finishing, not in net.
